changed_since_prior: AI-equity measures remain below their publication baselines even as the equal-weight annual return stays positive.
Electric-power construction accelerated while internal funding coverage edged higher.
Drought exposure widened across mapped campuses and associated published capacity.
Adoption-depth evidence now locates use within limited functions, tasks, and organizational change.
Published campus-capacity coverage clarifies the visibility gap between development scale and operating load.
confirming_signals: Operating cash flow covers current capital spending and cash reserves provide a near-term cushion.
The large interconnection queue and short operating-storage duration keep physical conversion central.
Business use remains concentrated across a few functions and tasks, with organizational adjustment partial.
Productivity growth continues to outpace real compensation, while labor gains remain narrow.
disconfirming_signals: Faster electric-power construction shows a stronger upstream supply response.
Retail electricity-price growth cooled while commercial and total demand grew.
The equal-weight equity return remains positive despite the market pullback.
analytical_state.thesis: Capital and grid construction are advancing faster than AI's conversion into broad business workflows and worker compensation.
unresolved_tensions: Advancement of queued projects and planned generation into operating, campus-delivered capacity.
Site-level connectivity and measured energized load across the campus pipeline.
Local water planning for campuses exposed to worsening county drought conditions.

Expansion from employee access into broader workflows and organizational redesign across businesses built around deeper operating integration over time while preserving gains for workers through stronger compensation growth alongside sustained productivity and output, with attention to whether infrastructure delivery, connectivity, power, and local water planning keep pace with campus development as projects advance from announced or queued status into operating assets capable of supporting reliable AI services at scale under varying regional conditions and whether current use across a limited set of functions and tasks broadens into durable process change that produces measurable performance gains and wider labor-market benefits across sectors, occupations, firms, and regions during subsequent evaluation cycles tracked under the same evidence discipline from funding through physical delivery, business use, workforce transmission, compensation, and realized economic outcomes.

decision_reason: Publication is mandatory because every published domain Read is stale under the run contract; the current capsules support a coherent update centered on faster upstream construction and slower downstream conversion.
